message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "# Reference:
#   - https://github.com/actions/checkout
#   - https://github.com/peter-evans/create-issue-from-file
#   - https://github.com/prefix-dev/setup-pixi

name: ci-spec-status

on:
  # no paths filter: the references job is a required check, and a required
  # check that never reports holds a pull request for ever, so the job decides
  # from what changed instead (ledger spec §3.7). A label re-runs it, as adding
  # "signed-off" is what a sign-off waits on.
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled, unlabeled]

  schedule:
    # every day @ 00h20
    - cron: "20 0 * * *"

  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  # a later run waits for the one in progress, and replaces any run still
  # waiting, which is dropped before its jobs start: a burst of label events,
  # as when a pull request opens with labels, then leaves no cancelled check
  # on it (#2915)
  cancel-in-progress: true

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash -l {0}

permissions: {}

jobs:
  references:
    # a status may cite the pull request that writes it, while still open
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    name: "status references"
    runs-on: "ubuntu-latest"

    env:
      # the files whose change changes this check, as globs
      WATCHED: |
        .github/scripts/breadcrumb.py
        .github/scripts/check_status_references.py
        .github/workflows/ci-spec-status.yml
        docs/src/_ext/geovista_citations.py
        docs/src/developer/specs/**
        tests/test_spec_conventions.py

    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: read
      pull-requests: read

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: "changed"
        id: changed
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          set -o errexit
          # NUL-delimited, as git quotes a non-ASCII name otherwise, and without
          # renames, so a specification moved away is seen by the path it left
          git diff --name-only -z --no-renames "${BASE_SHA}...${HEAD_SHA}" > changed.txt
          python3 - >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}" <<'PY'
          import fnmatch
          import os
          from pathlib import Path

          watched = os.environ["WATCHED"].split()
          changed = [p for p in Path("changed.txt").read_text().split("\0") if p]
          hit = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(path, glob) for path in changed for glob in watched)
          print(f"watched={'true' if hit else 'false'}")
          PY

      - name: "setup pixi"
        if: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.watched == 'true' }}
        uses: prefix-dev/setup-pixi@9936258fee697aff89b3fed6ca1f80a382ef694e
        with:
          environments: "test"
          frozen: true

      - name: "check status references"
        if: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.watched == 'true' }}
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          pixi run --frozen --environment test check-spec-status "${PR_NUMBER}"

  drift:
    # drift appears when other work lands, so look for it on main each night
    if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}
    name: "status drift"
    runs-on: "ubuntu-latest"

    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write  # required for peter-evans/create-issue-from-file
      pull-requests: read

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: "setup pixi"
        uses: prefix-dev/setup-pixi@9936258fee697aff89b3fed6ca1f80a382ef694e
        with:
          environments: "test"
          frozen: true

      - name: "check status drift"
        id: check
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          status=0
          pixi run --frozen --environment test check-spec-status drift > status.txt 2>&1 || status=$?
          cat status.txt
          {
            echo "The nightly check of the specification statuses found the work they"
            echo "cite has moved on, or is not what they say. Run"
            echo "\`pixi run -e test check-spec-status drift\` to reproduce it."
            echo
            echo '```'
            grep -v -e "^Why this check exists" -e "#gv-developer-checks-" status.txt || true
            echo '```'
            echo
            # the breadcrumb is left out of the fence, so its link can be followed
            grep -A1 "^Why this check exists" status.txt || true
          } > status.md
          echo "exit_code=${status}" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"

      # exit code 2 is GitHub being unreachable, which is not worth an issue
      - name: "report failure"
        if: ${{ steps.check.outputs.exit_code == '1' }}
        uses: peter-evans/create-issue-from-file@fca9117c27cdc29c6c4db3b86c48e4115a786710
        with:
          title: "chore: specification status drift"
          content-filepath: ./status.md
          labels: |
            bot
            new: issue
            type: documentation

      - name: "exit action"
        if: ${{ steps.check.outputs.exit_code != '0' }}
        env:
          EXIT_CODE: ${{ steps.check.outputs.exit_code }}
        run: |
          exit "${EXIT_CODE}"
",
  "rationale": "The workflow currently sets `cancel-in-progress: false` in its concurrency configuration, causing superseded runs (e.g., rapid pushes to the same PR) to queue and all execute. Pattern P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE documents that canceling superseded runs for the same workflow and branch/PR reduces duplicate work (estimated 1.9% free / 4.1% paid VM time reduction). The workflow's concurrency group `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` already partitions by workflow and ref (branch/PR), satisfying the pattern's preconditions. The change is minimal, preserves all required checks and coverage, and does not affect the schedule/dispatch drift job's isolation from PR runs. No contraindications apply (not release/deployment work; distinct branches have distinct refs).",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE"]
}
message.reasoning:
Let me analyze this workflow and the evidence to determine if there's a suitable CI optimization.

The workflow is `ci-spec-status.yml` which:
1. Runs on pull_request events (opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled, unlabeled)
2. Runs on schedule (daily at 00:20)
3. Runs on workflow_dispatch

It has two jobs:
1. `references` - runs on pull_request events, checks status references
2. `drift` - runs on non-pull_request events (schedule, workflow_dispatch), checks for specification drift

Key observations:
- The workflow uses `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: false` - meaning it doesn't cancel in-progress runs
- The `references` job only runs if watched files changed
- The `drift` job runs nightly and creates issues if drift is found
- Uses `prefix-dev/setup-pixi` for environment setup
- Uses `peter-evans/create-issue-from-file` for reporting drift

Now let me look at the evidence patterns to see what might apply:

1. **P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE** - Cancel superseded runs. The workflow has `cancel-in-progress: false` which means it doesn't cancel stale runs. This could be applicable since multiple PR updates could queue up runs.

2. **P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE** - Suppress schedules during repository inactivity. The workflow runs daily on schedule. If there's no activity, this could be suppressed.

3. **P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE** - Pause repeatedly failing scheduled workflows. The schedule runs daily and could fail repeatedly.

4. **P-LIT-GHA-CACHE** - Cache dependency downloads. The workflow uses pixi with `frozen: true` which suggests dependencies are locked.

5. **P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER** - The workflow already has a change filter for the `references` job (it checks if watched files changed).

Let me check the preconditions and contraindications for each:

**P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE**:
- Preconditions: "Runs represent the same workflow and branch or PR", "A newer revision supersedes older checks"
- Contraindications: "Release or deployment work", "Distinct branches share a cancellation group"
- This workflow is not release/deployment work. It runs on PRs and schedule. For PRs, newer commits supersede older ones. The concurrency group is `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` which is per workflow and ref (branch/PR). This seems applicable.

**P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE**:
- Preconditions: "Periodic results depend only on repository changes"
- Contraindications: "External dependencies, security or time-based requirements need fresh checks"
- The drift check compares specifications against cited work. If the repository hasn't changed, the drift check would likely produce the same result. However, the cited work could have changed externally. The workflow checks "specification statuses found the work they cite has moved on" - this suggests external dependencies. So this might not be applicable due to contraindications.

**P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE**:
- Preconditions: "A monitored pause/resume policy is approved"
- Contraindications: "Continuous monitoring or periodic checks are mandatory"
- This is a periodic check for drift. It might be considered mandatory monitoring. Also, there's no mention of a pause/resume policy being approved.

**P-LIT-GHA-CACHE**:
- Preconditions: "Repeated dependency fetching is measurable", "Cache inputs include lockfile and environment"
- The workflow uses pixi with frozen environments. Pixi likely has its own caching. The setup-pixi action might already handle caching. Need to check if there's measurable repeated dependency fetching.

Looking at the workflow, it uses `prefix-dev/setup-pixi` with `frozen: true` and `environments: "test"`. The pixi tool itself manages dependencies and likely caches them. The setup-pixi action may also cache the pixi installation. This might already be optimized.

**P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER**: Already implemented for the references job.

**P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT**: Could be applicable but no evidence of runaway jobs.

**P-LIT-FAIL-FAST**: No matrix jobs in this workflow.

The most promising seems to be **P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE** for the PR runs. The workflow currently has `cancel-in-progress: false` which means if someone pushes multiple commits quickly, multiple runs will queue up and all run. Since the `references` job only runs when watched files change, and newer commits supersede older ones for the same PR, canceling the previous run would save resources.

Let me verify the concurrency group: `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` - this groups by workflow and ref (branch/PR). For a PR, the ref is `refs/pull/<number>/merge` or similar, so all runs for the same PR would be in the same group. Setting `cancel-in-progress: true` would cancel the previous run when a new one starts for the same PR.

This matches the pattern P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE:
- "Runs represent the same workflow and branch or PR" ✓
- "A newer revision supersedes older checks" ✓ (for PRs, the latest commit is what matters)
- Not release/deployment work ✓
- Distinct branches don't share a cancellation group (each PR/branch has its own ref) ✓

The evidence shows this pattern has estimated benefit: "Superseding runs can reduce duplicate work" with "vm_time_reduction_percent": {"free": 1.9, "paid": 4.1}.

I should propose changing `cancel-in-progress: false` to `cancel-in-progress: true` in the concurrency section.

Let me also check if there are any safety concerns. The workflow has two jobs: `references` (PR only) and `drift` (schedule/dispatch only). They run on different triggers, so they won't interfere with each other's concurrency. The concurrency group includes the ref, so schedule runs (which run on main branch) would have a different ref than PR runs.

Actually, wait. For schedule events, the ref is the default branch (main). For workflow_dispatch, it's also the default branch or the specified ref. So schedule and workflow_dispatch runs would share the same concurrency group if they run on the same branch. But the workflow has `if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}` for drift and `if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}` for references. So they're mutually exclusive by event type. But if a schedule run is in progress and a workflow_dispatch happens, they'd be in the same concurrency group (same workflow, same ref=main). With `cancel-in-progress: true`, the workflow_dispatch would cancel the schedule run or vice versa.

Is that desirable? The drift job creates issues for specification drift. If a manual dispatch cancels a scheduled run, that might be okay since the manual run would do the same check. But if a scheduled run cancels a manual run, that might be less desirable. However, the pattern says "A newer revision supersedes older checks" - for schedule vs dispatch on the same branch, they're the same revision (both on main), so neither supersedes the other. But the pattern is about "superseded runs" - a newer run of the same workflow on the same ref.

Actually, looking at the pattern more carefully: "Partition cancellation by workflow and branch/PR" and "Preserve run identity and audit records". The concurrency group already partitions by workflow and ref. The question is whether cancel-in-progress is appropriate.

For PRs: definitely yes, newer commits supersede older ones.
For schedule/dispatch on main: they're the same revision, so canceling might not be "superseding" but rather "duplicate". But the pattern says "Superseding runs can reduce duplicate work" - duplicate work is also reduced.

The contraindication "Distinct branches share a cancellation group" doesn't apply because the group includes the ref.

I think this is a safe and supported change. Let me prepare the updated workflow.

The only change needed is in the concurrency section:
```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true  # changed from false
```

This is a minimal change that preserves all build and test coverage, and is supported by evidence P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE.

Let me also check if there's any other optimization. The workflow already has change filtering for the references job. The drift job runs on schedule and could potentially use P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE, but the contraindication about external dependencies applies (the drift check looks for external changes in cited work).

So I'll go with P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE.
